adjudication_records.issue_text: config/routes.rb:439 — Unsubscribe is a state-changing GET that bypasses CSRF protection and can be triggered cross-site, by prefetching, or by authenticated link scanners

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows a new GET route at 'get "t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe" => "topics#unsubscribe"' in config/routes.rb. The controller action in topics_controller.rb modifies state by changing tu.notification_level and calling tu.save!. This is a state-changing operation on a GET request. The controller adds :unsubscribe to skip_before_filter :verify_authenticity_token (via the ensure_logged_in list) and skip_before_filter :check_xhr. GET requests with state changes are vulnerable to CSRF attacks, link prefetching by browsers, and authenticated link scanners that may automatically visit URLs in emails - which is exactly how this unsubscribe link is delivered (via email as shown in user_notifications.rb adding unsubscribe_url to emails).

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:108 — Unsubscribe is not idempotent: retries change watched/tracked topics from regular to muted, unexpectedly hiding them and suppressing mentions

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows the unsubscribe action at lines 98-113 in topics_controller.rb. The logic is: if notification_level > regular, set to regular; else set to muted. This means if a user clicks unsubscribe once on a watched/tracked topic, it becomes regular. If they click again (retry/refresh), since regular is not > regular, it will be set to muted. This is indeed not idempotent - repeated clicks change behavior unexpectedly, potentially muting topics and hiding them from the user when they only intended to stop notifications.
